title: Ideal conductor
body: A material in which electrons are able to move freely.
ced_evidence: 10.1.A.1 "An ideal conductor is a material in which electrons are able to move freely."

title: Conductor in electrostatic equilibrium: required properties
body: Properties a student must state or apply for a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium.

items.label: Excess charge on the surface
items.meaning: Mutual repulsion puts all excess charge carriers on the conductor's surface; the interior has no net charge.

items.label: Zero field inside
items.meaning: The electric field is zero within the conductor.

items.label: Field perpendicular to the surface
items.meaning: The electric field is perpendicular to the outer surface of the conductor.

items.label: Equipotential
items.meaning: All points on the surface have the same electric potential, so the conductor is an equipotential surface.

items.label: Greater charge density at points and edges
items.meaning: Surface charge density is greater at points or edges than on planar areas.

items.label: Negligible equilibrium time
items.meaning: The time for charges to reach equilibrium is so short as to be negligible.

ced_evidence: 10.1.A.2, 10.1.A.3.i-iii, 10.1.A.4, 10.1.A.5 "charge carriers residing entirely on the surface"

title: Modeling charge on a positively charged conductor
body: A positively charged conductor's surface is deficient in electrons, and this is modeled as positive charge carriers residing on the surface.
ced_evidence: 10.1.A.2.ii "can be modeled as if positive charge carriers reside on the surface"

title: Polarization of a conductor
body: A conductor in an external electric field becomes polarized as a consequence of remaining an equipotential surface.
ced_evidence: 10.1.A.6 "A conductor can be polarized in the presence of an external electric field"

title: Electrostatic shielding
body: Surrounding an area with a closed, conducting shell to create a region inside that is free from external electric fields.
ced_evidence: 10.1.A.7 "Electrostatic shielding is the process of surrounding an area with a closed, conducting shell"

title: Conductors in electrical contact
body: When conductors are in electrical contact, charge redistributes until the surfaces of each conductor are at the same electric potential.
caution: The conductors end up at equal potential, not necessarily with equal charge.
ced_evidence: 10.2.A.1 "surfaces of each conductor are at the same electric potential"

title: Ground
body: An idealized reference point with zero electric potential that can absorb or provide an infinite amount of charge without changing its electric potential.
ced_evidence: 10.2.A.2 "Ground is an idealized reference point that has zero electric potential"

title: Inducing charge by grounding
body: Charge can be induced on a conductor by grounding it in the presence of an external electric field.
ced_evidence: 10.2.A.3 "Charge can be induced on a conductor by grounding the conductor"

title: Parallel-plate capacitor
body: Two separated parallel conducting surfaces that can hold equal amounts of charge with opposite signs.
ced_evidence: 10.3.A.1 "two separated parallel conducting surfaces"

title: Definition of capacitance
body: C = \frac{Q}{\Delta V}
caution: Q is the magnitude of charge on each plate, not the net charge on the capacitor, which is zero.
ced_evidence: 10.3.A.2 "Capacitance relates the magnitude of the charge stored on each plate to the electric potential difference"

title: What capacitance depends on
body: Capacitance depends only on the capacitor's physical properties, such as its shape and the material separating the plates, not on Q or ΔV.
ced_evidence: 10.3.A.2.i "depends only on the physical properties of the capacitor"

title: Parallel-plate capacitance
body: C = \frac{\kappa \varepsilon_0 A}{d}
caution: This formula applies only to parallel plates. For spherical or cylindrical capacitors, re-derive C = Q/ΔV from that geometry's own Q and ΔV. Substituting cylinder or sphere surface areas into this formula is a documented error.
ced_evidence: 10.3.A.2.ii "proportional to the area of one of its plates and inversely proportional to the distance between its plates"

title: Capacitor geometries requiring quantitative analysis
body: The only capacitor geometries expected for quantitative analysis and description.
ced_evidence: Boundary statement: "parallel-plate capacitors, concentric spherical capacitors, and coaxial cylindrical capacitors"

title: Field between parallel plates
body: E = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0 A}
caution: Valid where the plate separation is much smaller than the plate dimensions, away from the edges. It comes from Gauss's law plus superposition.
ced_evidence: 10.3.A.3.i "determined by applying Gauss's law and the principle of superposition"

title: Field and motion between parallel plates
body: The field between uniformly charged parallel plates is constant in magnitude and direction except near the edges, is proportional to the surface charge density, and gives a charged particle constant acceleration like projectile motion in gravity.
ced_evidence: 10.3.A.3, 10.3.A.3.ii, 10.3.A.3.iii "constant acceleration"

title: Energy stored in a capacitor
body: U_C = \frac{1}{2} Q \Delta V
caution: The stored energy equals the work done by an external force to separate that charge.
ced_evidence: 10.3.A.4-5 "equal to the work done by an external force to separate that amount of charge"

title: Dielectric material
body: A material in which electric charges are not as free to move as in a conductor, and which becomes polarized in the presence of an external electric field.
ced_evidence: 10.4.A.1 "becomes polarized in the presence of an external electric field"

title: Dielectric constant
body: \kappa = \frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon_0}
ced_evidence: 10.4.A.2 "relates the electric permittivity of that material to the permittivity of free space"

title: Field of a polarized dielectric
body: The electric field created by a polarized dielectric is opposite in direction to the external field.
ced_evidence: 10.4.A.3 "opposite in direction to the external field"

title: Field reduction with a dielectric
body: \kappa = \frac{E_0}{E}
caution: This applies to an isolated parallel-plate capacitor (constant Q), where the field decreases when a dielectric is inserted.
ced_evidence: 10.4.A.4 "decreases when a dielectric is placed between the plates"

title: Capacitance with a dielectric
body: C = \kappa C_0
ced_evidence: 10.4.A.5 "insertion of a dielectric into a capacitor may change the capacitance"
